JUDGMENT
In both these writ petitions petitioners are proprietors of hotels who are issued with license under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

In the case of petitioner in WP(C) No.2467 of 2015 it is stated that after expiry of the license the petitioner had applied for renewal as per Ext.P2 chalan Unknown vs By Advs.Sri.C.S.Ajith Prakash on 4 December, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95404871/
2 dated 04.2.2013.

The grievance of the petitioners is against the notice issued by the Special Squad of Food Safety Officers imposing fine of Rs.25,000/- and 13,000/- respectively pointing out certain defects as mentioned in those notices.
The writ petitions were filed challenging these notices alleging that it is in violation of the provisions contained in Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
It is also alleged that officers who issued notices do not have any authority to impose any fine or to compound the offences.
It is also pointed out that no notices were issued to the petitioners before the fine was imposed.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioners points out that similar issue has already been considered by this Court in the common judgment dated 22.11.2014 in WP(C) No.18743 of 2012 and W.P.(C)
Nos.2467 & 2468 of 2015 connected cases.
It was found that the respondents had not served any notice on the petitioners under section 32 of the Act for improvement and compounding was ordered without any request from petitioners.

It was found that the designated officer has to send the food samples for proper analysis and report with a copy to the Commissioner of Food Safety and it is only after complying with the procedure that the adjudicating officer or the court can impose penalty or punishment on offenders and therefore compounding of offences was held to be in violation of the procedure prescribed under the Act.
Therefore those writ petitions were allowed leaving it open for the authorities to proceed against the petitioners therein in accordance with law.
3. I heard the learned Government Pleader also.
4. It is seen that notices which are impugned in these writ petitions Exts.P3 and P2 respectively are issued in violation of rule 32 of the Rules as well as rule 69 of the Act.
Petitioners have stated that there was no prior notice and that the sample was not collected or analysed before issuing the impugned notices.

In the above circumstances, in the light of the judgment dated 22.11.2014 in WP(C) No.18743 of 2012 and connected cases the notice-Ext.P3 issued in WP(C) No.2467 of 2015 and Ext.P2 notice W.P.(C) Nos.2467 & 2468 of 2015 issued in WP(C) No.2468 of 2015 are set aside.
Respondents would be free to proceed against the petitioners, if warranted so, in accordance with law.

sd/-
P.V.ASHA JUDGE rkc
